topic: Historical replay (2026-09-12 snapshot): search and adaptive retrieval

papers.why_it_matters: The pinned August revision studies a model that learns multi-turn search during reasoning. Its retrieval-token masking and outcome reward are concrete design variables to investigate for the Envoy worker; they are not proof of transfer to a personal vault.

evidence.quote: Search-R1 optimizes LLM reasoning trajectories with multi-turn search interactions
leveraging retrieved token masking for stable RL training and a simple outcome-based reward function

limitations: The reported results use seven question-answering datasets, not this Obsidian corpus or our exact-span support metric.
A historical August 2025 replay does not establish this is newly relevant in September 2026.
This extract does not compare v4 with v5, so it does not establish what changed in the revision or whether the change was substantive.

related_notes.reason: Retrospective comparison with the later local pilot that questioned whether an iterative worker earns its extra cost; the pilot was not caused by this paper.

papers.context_reason: An older reference for interleaving reasoning with external actions, useful for contrasting prompted tool use with the later Search-R1 training setup.
papers.why_it_matters: ReAct gives a baseline pattern for alternating model reasoning and information-gathering actions, relevant to the existing search/read/extract harness.

evidence.quote: generate both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner
actions allow it to interface with external sources

limitations: It does not demonstrate that the current Qwen checkpoint improves personal-vault answer support.

related_notes.reason: Retrospective link to the later idea of testing repeated search against a one-pass baseline; the note does not claim to cite ReAct.

papers.context_reason: An older reference for selecting among no retrieval, single-step retrieval, and iterative retrieval by question complexity.
papers.why_it_matters: Adaptive-RAG motivates measuring whether a cheaper routing decision can avoid multi-step retrieval on straightforward questions.

evidence.quote: simple queries with unnecessary computational overhead
between the iterative and single-step retrieval-augmented LLMs, as well as the no-retrieval methods

limitations: Its complexity labels and benchmark mix do not establish a suitable router for this personal-vault workload.

related_notes.reason: Retrospective comparison with the later plan to use cheap lexical retrieval by default and Qwen only for questions that need more investigation.

next_measurement: On the same future held-out personal-vault question IDs and frozen snapshot, compare BM25 as a retrieval/evidence baseline. Compare base Qwen3-8B and v5 under identical tool access, decoding, and answer budget. Human-review their supported answers and record execution failures, latency, tokens, and GPU cost. Stop if v5 adds no supported coverage.
analysis_note: This retrospective selection was drafted from abstracts and selected passages; the full HTML papers and version-to-version changes were not reviewed end to end.
